one_liner: Java port of Lemire's SIMD Quad search: quaternary narrowing plus a Vector API block scan, 5-29% lower mean latency than Arrays.binarySearch on int arrays.
what_it_does: Two static methods, QuadSearch.search(int[], int) and SimdQuadSearch.search(int[], int), look up a value in a sorted int[] and return the same encoding as Arrays.binarySearch: the index if found, otherwise -(insertion point) - 1. It is a ~100-line source drop with no Maven artifact or release, adapted from the C++ uint16 membership test in Lemire's 'You can beat the binary search' post (catalogued in wave 1 as SIMD Quad search) to int keys and insertion-point results. A third class, BranchlessQuadSearch, is an unbenchmarked experiment that returns -1 instead of the insertion point.
how_it_is_fast: The array is treated as 16-int blocks. A quaternary (4-ary) search over the block-end keys loads three independent pivots per step, so their cache misses overlap (memory-level parallelism) and the chain of dependent loads drops from about log2(n) to about log4(n/16) levels. Once one to three blocks remain, SimdQuadSearch scans the 16-int block with IntVector.compare(GE) at SPECIES_PREFERRED width (4 lanes on NEON, 8 on AVX2), turns the mask into a long and takes numberOfTrailingZeros, which yields the found index or the insertion point without a per-element branch.
when_to_use: Hot lookup loops over sorted int[] of 4k to 1M elements (posting lists, sorted column chunks, many small sorted arrays) on JDK 25 where a 10-25% cut in mean lookup time matters.

Cold-cache lookups across many arrays, where the quaternary step overlaps cache misses: amd64 Oracle JDK 1m cold measured 1053.8 ns for simdQuadSearch and 1020.1 ns for the scalar QuadSearch vs 1192.8 ns for Arrays.binarySearch.
x86-64 deployments that cannot enable incubator modules: the scalar QuadSearch needs no jdk.incubator.vector and already beat binarySearch in the amd64 cells cited.
As readable reference code for porting the SIMD Quad idea to other JVM key types (long, float) with Arrays.binarySearch result semantics.
when_not_to_use: On arm64 without the SIMD variant: the scalar QuadSearch was slower than Arrays.binarySearch at 4k to 16k cold (arm64 Oracle 4k cold 130.9 vs 110.5 ns) and at 4k warm (37.4 vs 32.5 ns).
On GraalVM at some sizes the SIMD variant loses (amd64 GraalVM 16k warm 206.2 vs 197.2 ns; arm64 GraalVM 4k warm 34.4 vs 33.4 ns); measure on your JVM before switching.
Code that cannot ship with --add-modules jdk.incubator.vector: the Vector API is still incubating and can change between JDK releases.
Arrays under 4k elements (not benchmarked; under 16 elements it is a plain linear scan), long[]/double[]/Object[] with a Comparator, or fromIndex/toIndex range searches: none are provided.
Teams wanting a maintained library: 3 stars, 12 commits over 2026-05-23 to 2026-05-25, no releases, no artifact.

integration.dependencies: none for QuadSearch; SimdQuadSearch needs the jdk.incubator.vector module (--add-modules jdk.incubator.vector at compile and run time)
integration.min_toolchain: Java 25 as built and benchmarked (Gradle toolchain languageVersion 25; build also passes --enable-preview); earlier JDKs with the Vector API incubator are untested
integration.platforms: any JVM; benchmarked on Apple M4 (NEON, 128-bit) and an unnamed AMD x86-64 CPU (AVX2, 256-bit) with Oracle JDK and GraalVM
integration.thread_safety: stateless static methods that only read the array; safe for concurrent readers (from source, not documented)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same (int[], int) call shape and return encoding as Arrays.binarySearch for sorted int arrays, but no range, long, float, double or Object overloads; with duplicates it returns the leftmost match where Arrays.binarySearch returns any match; SimdQuadSearch needs the incubator module

gotchas: Harness flaw on arm64: JMH SampleTime times single calls, and the arm64 files show percentiles in ~41.7 ns steps (Oracle 4k warm: p0 ~0, p50 41, p90 42, p95 83 or 125 ns) while the means are 24 to 37 ns, so each sample is at or below one timer tick; the small-size means are averages of quantized readings and the README's 'p99 better almost in all test cases' compares tick multiples (83 vs 166 ns). On amd64 every sample carries a floor (p0 = 29 ns in each file read) that dilutes, rather than inflates, the reported gains.

Workload skew: queries are uniform in [0, 8n) while the arrays end near 4.5n on average, so about 44% of queries are past the last element; for those the SIMD block scan never runs and both algorithms walk the same rightmost path. 'Warm' means 128 consecutive queries per array (README says 100) over a 4 GB array set, so the first queries on each array are still cold.

No result cross-check: the benchmark returns results to JMH without comparing them, and the Spock tests use arrays of at most 51 elements, so the quaternary loop (it only runs with more than 3 blocks, i.e. 64+ elements) is never tested. Reading the loop, its invariant holds (the target is at most the end key of block hi unless hi is the last block, and the remainder tail is scanned linearly), so no correctness bug was found.

blockSearch assumes the preferred vector holds at most 16 ints and divides 16 (true for NEON, AVX2 and AVX-512); on a wider vector length IntVector.fromArray on the final block would read past the array end and throw.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No sibling in this category is a search routine; the closest catalogued work is Lemire's C++ SIMD Quad search (wave 1, searching), which this ports to Java. Pick this one when you are on the JVM and need Arrays.binarySearch's insertion-point result; use Lemire's C++ code for uint16 membership tests in native code.
verified_claims_summary: First-party JMH 1.37 runs (SampleTime, 3 forks, 5 x 2 s warmup, 10 x 2 s measurement, -Xmx12g G1) on Java 25 Oracle JDK and GraalVM, on an Apple M4 and an unnamed AMD AVX2 machine, search sorted int arrays of 4k to 1M elements in cold and 128-query warm modes; simdQuadSearch's mean ns/op is typically 5-15% below Arrays.binarySearch, at best 24.7% (arm64 Oracle 4k warm, 24.5 vs 32.5 ns) and 29.3% (amd64 GraalVM 8k cold, 466.6 vs 659.6 ns), and slower in a few GraalVM cells. All 72 result files are in docs/results.
status_note: Weekend experiment from May 2026 (Apache-2.0, 3 stars, 12 commits, no release or artifact); small enough to copy, but SimdQuadSearch ties you to the incubating Vector API and the code has no tests at sizes where the quaternary loop runs.
